OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: FY2026E CPO-equivalent sales of 1,045kt: the FY2025 revenue-implied volume was 941kt [F59], and SML (11,046 ha, young palms, completed 24 November 2025) consolidates for a full year, lifting own output and third-party throughput; 9M2026 revenue growth of 34.85% [S7] is consistent with that step-up on a higher CPO price and FX. Growth fades to 1.4%/yr by FY2030 as the young-planting uplift annualises, then volume is held flat. The level is derived, not disclosed: F59 is the revenue line divided by the benchmark, FX and the realisation, so the unit cost - cash cost over that volume - inherits the same denominator. We therefore do not rest the valuation on it silently: the second sensitivity grid prices volume against cost intensity (a fifth fewer tonnes on the same cash cost is a quarter higher unit cost), and the product-level sales and trading volume that would replace the derived figure are recorded as an archive evidence gap because no registered source discloses them.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: 0.95 of the CPO benchmark, calibrated on the FY2025 actual: revenue of Rp14.81tn at the FY2025 benchmark of US$1,007/t and average FX of 16,448 implies a realised ASP of US$956.65/t, a 5% wedge. This is the empirical revenue netback, not a forecast haircut: it is measured after every deduction the company actually took in the year, but it is NOT 'benchmark less the statutory levy', and the full statutory charge is not inside it. The deck is a pre-levy international reference series, and the November 2026 combined duty and levy of USD246.36/t [S29] is 21.7% of the FY2026E benchmark and 24.5% of the FY2025 benchmark, between four and five times the 5% wedge, so a wedge that small cannot be the statutory deduction. What the wedge embeds is the average fiscal incidence across the tonnes actually sold, and the disclosed accounts bound that rather than reveal it: a seller that kept 95% of the benchmark cannot have borne more than USD50.4/t of charge on its whole sold volume at the FY2025 benchmark (5% of USD1,007), at most about a fifth of the headline rate, with freight, product mix and the domestic reference price accounting for the rest of the wedge. The incidence is small because the charge falls on exported tonnes only and part of it is competed back into the third-party FFB price the mill pays. SSMS does not disclose its export/domestic split, so the wedge cannot be decomposed into freight, product, domestic mix and levy incidence; that is stated as an evidence gap, not filled with an estimate. The pair is stable on any reading: a levy-netback reading would require roughly a fifth more volume, more than half of it resale, which the physical chain (527kt own CPO, 104kt kernel, 15kt PKO) does not support [F2][F4][F5], and deducting the headline rate as a separate line would cut revenue by a fifth and contradict the reported line. Volume and realisation are jointly identified from the revenue line, so the pair is anchored to the actual year. Held flat; the November relief is not capitalised (see cost_per_bcm).

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No price cap applies to palm oil; the domestic-market obligation is a sales-allocation rule, not a capped price.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Cost-intensity factor of 1.0: one tonne of CPO-equivalent sold consumes one unit of cost_per_bcm, so cost_per_bcm is the all-in cash cost per tonne and there is no separate mining ratio.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: FY2026 base cash cost of Rp10.44m/t, set so that the full unit cost at the FY2026 benchmark reproduces the 9M2026 actual of Rp10.75m/t: 9M2026 COGS of Rp8,890bn less D&A of Rp473bn is Rp8,417bn of cash cost on the 9M volume the revenue line implies (784kt, itself derived from revenue and disclosed as derived in volume, with the volume-versus-cost-intensity sensitivity grid pricing the denominator). The step from the FY2025 actual of Rp9.64m/t (+8.3%, +11.5% at the 9M price) decomposes into two disclosed legs and no unexplained residual: (i) the price-and-FX-linked purchased-feed slice, 23.5% of the cost base, against the 9M2026 benchmark of USD1,131 (12.3% above FY2025) and FX 6.8% higher, so the IDR cost of bought fruit rose 19.9% and contributes 4.7pp; (ii) rupiah inflation at 2.5%/yr over two years on the 76.5% own-estate slice, 3.8pp. The SML consolidation is what puts a young estate with a higher cost per tonne into the mix, and it is inside the own-estate slice rather than a separate leg. The FY2025 base of Rp10.25m/t is superseded because it reproduced the FY2025 year, not the FY2026 run-rate. It grows 2.5%/yr with IDR inflation; the CPO-linked share is added by the fuel term. The levy: the charge actually borne at the 9M2026 level is already inside the reported revenue and cost lines, while the full statutory schedule is not (see realisation for the bound); the November 2026 relief is not capitalised into FY2027E because the charge resets monthly off a reference price that the deck's own FY2027E price path implies is higher [S29]. If the relief held all year on the whole volume it would be worth up to USD61.91/t, about Rp1,137bn of revenue equivalent on FY2026E volume at the deck FX; we show it as a monitored upside rather than a base-case drift.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: 23.5% is the purchased-feed share of throughput: third-party FFB of 516kt plus plasma FFB of 44.4kt against 2,383kt processed [F19][F62][F6]. That is the share of the cost base whose price tracks the CPO benchmark, so the template's price-link term passes the benchmark through to that slice; the remaining 76.5% is own-estate cost that moves with inflation. The earlier 60% was not sourced to the physical purchased share and is withdrawn.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Zero: all cash cost is carried in cost_per_bcm so the unit cost is not double counted.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Zero, and not because the levy is hidden in the wedge. Palm oil carries no output-based royalty: there is no concession or licence schedule, and the Indonesian export levy and duty (November 2026 bea keluar USD124/t plus pungutan ekspor USD122.36/t, USD246.36/t in total [S29]) is a fiscal charge on the exported tonne, not a royalty on production. The revenue side of the model is the reported revenue line, which is already after whatever charge was actually paid, and the cost base is the reported nine-month cost: that is why neither a royalty nor a levy line is added, because a second deduction would double count, and not because the wedge equals the statutory charge, which it cannot at more than four times the wedge's size (see realisation for the bound). The charge is set monthly against the Kemendag reference price [S29], which is why the model holds it at the level the 9M2026 accounts earned rather than forecasting the November schedule forward.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: No separate other-revenue line is disclosed; the revenue build covers CPO, olein, CPKO and palm kernel.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: No other revenue, so the margin is not used.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Rp604k/t for FY2026. The cash-flow identity implies FY2025 D&A of about Rp568bn (CFO of Rp1,097bn less net profit of Rp1,203bn plus the Rp674bn working-capital build), or Rp604k per revenue-implied tonne; the data pack's Rp73bn depreciation line is the G&A-only figure and is not used. D&A grows with inflation as the asset base expands.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Rp700k/t for FY2026: FY2025 capex of Rp475bn on 941kt was Rp505k/t, lifted for SML development, replanting and mill/infrastructure spend funded by the Rp5.2tn syndicated facility [S13]; it grows with inflation.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: No separately costed expansion project is disclosed; growth capex is carried in capex_unit.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue)); FY2025 operating NWC of Rp3.18tn is 21.5% of revenue, consistent with the default

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 effective tax is 24.7% (Rp575.09bn on Rp2.33tn pre-tax profit), close to the 22% statutory rate plus local taxes; 25% is held through the forecast.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 6.5%, the filing's effective rate, not a 9% placeholder. Operating profit of Rp2.76tn less pre-tax profit of Rp2.33tn leaves Rp0.43tn of net finance cost and associate income combined [S7]; annualised that is about Rp0.57tn against opening debt of Rp8.42tn, or 6.8%, and against average debt near Rp9tn, 6.4%. On the opening debt the engine charges interest against, 6.5% reproduces the observed annualised charge. The cost of debt input governs the interest line, the payout cover and the cash build, not the DCF, which is unlevered; the WACC's kd is the house floor at rf plus 200bp and is not moved by this input, a stated conservatism explained in section 4.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E borrowing of Rp3,606bn takes year-end gross debt from the FY2025A Rp8,423bn to the 30 September 2026 actual of Rp12,029bn and assumes no net repayment in the fourth quarter: the balance sheet already carries the SML purchase and the dividend, and the Rp3.2tn DHE placement is the company's own export proceeds locked onshore for up to twelve months [S31], which is why the cash line holds up. The old path added Rp900bn and ended FY2026E at Rp9,323bn, Rp2.7tn below the September actual, which implied an implausible fourth-quarter repayment; it is withdrawn. No further net borrowing after FY2026E: capex and the dividend are covered by operating cash flow from FY2027E.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: no recurring non-operating item is disclosed and associate income is not forecast. The engine's EBIT is revenue less cost of revenue less opex, so no associate earnings are in the cash flow, and the associate is instead carried at its 30 September 2026 book line in the bridge (see valuation.bridge). Carrying both a book value and an earnings stream would double count.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 minority share of profit is 9.14% (Rp1.75tn total versus Rp1.59tn attributable), up from 3.3% in FY2025 as SML (63.4% owned) consolidates; 9.1% is used for the forecast, the actual rather than a lower placeholder.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 65% of parent earnings: FY2025 paid 68.92% (Rp800bn) [S12] and the FY2026 interim is Rp500bn or Rp52.49 per share [S3]; 65% keeps the dividend slightly below the FY2025 ratio as capex rises.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No issuance, buyback or split announced; the register is 9,525m shares.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.5% nominal in IDR, the deck's own long-run escalation and therefore the growth the forecast actually delivers: from FY2030E the long-run CPO marker (fund record d.agri.cpo, lt 1150, lt_escalation idr) escalates at 2.5%/yr, the cost base escalates at 2.5%/yr and volume is capped at the FY2030E level, so FCFF grows at about 2.5% in the tail. The withdrawn 4.0% capitalised roughly 1.5pp of perpetual margin expansion the explicit forecast does not earn, and it sat above both the model's own FY2035E FCFF growth and the only PLANTATIONS peer's rate. 2.5% is below long-run rupiah inflation, so real CPO prices decline in perpetuity, which is the conservative side of the same consistency.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 21.44% of revenue, the 9M2026 actual: revenue of Rp14,830bn less cost of revenue of Rp8,890bn less operating profit of Rp2,760bn leaves Rp3,180bn of SG&A and selling cost, or 21.4%. Decomposition of the step from FY2025's 18.5%: SG&A per tonne of sold volume rose from Rp2.91m to Rp4.06m, +39%, against a 20% rise in revenue per tonne. A cost that were purely proportional to the dollar selling price would have left the ratio unchanged, and rupiah inflation at 2.5%/yr over two years accounts for 5.1pp of the 39%; the rest is the volume- and mix-driven leg — SML's overhead consolidated for a full year and the purchased-product resale mix — which the archive does not disclose separately. We state that residual as an evidence gap rather than dress it up: the archive carries no SG&A note. The 9M run-rate is the anchor for FY2026 and is carried flat rather than mean-reverted to the lower FY2025 price base, because the FY2025 ratio was earned at a benchmark 11% lower.

challenges.challenge: The report states that Indonesia's CPO export levy and duty are 'embedded in the 0.95 realisation wedge' [S11, S16]. Neither source contains the word levy or pungutan, and the arithmetic cannot work: the packet's own news file puts total CPO export levy and duty at USD246.36/t in November 2026, which is 21.7% of the USD1,135/t FY2026E benchmark, while the entire wedge is 5%, or USD56.75/t. Either d.agri.cpo is a post-levy domestic reference series (in which case say so and re-read the FY2027E path) or realisations are understated by about 17%. The claim is the stated reason royalty_rate is zero and the wedge is held flat.
challenges.answer: The deck is a pre-levy World Bank Pink Sheet series (Malaysia crude/RBD) that carries no Indonesian fiscal charge, and the report no longer says the levy sits inside a 5% wedge. Section 2 now carries the November schedule from S29 (bea keluar 124 plus pungutan 122.36, total 246.36 a tonne, against a 978.90 reference), states that the wedge is the empirical revenue netback the accounts delivered rather than benchmark less levy, and bounds the levy incidence by the disclosed revenue and unit cash cost because SSMS does not publish an export/domestic split. royalty_rate stays zero because palm oil pays no royalty: the levy is a fiscal charge carried inside the netback and cost lines, not deducted twice.

challenges.challenge: The November 2026 cut in total CPO export levy and duty from USD308.27 to USD246.36/t (news 2026-11-06, flagged material) is absent from the report, and the model holds realisation at 0.95 with no sensitivity to it. At 1,045kt and Rp17,570/USD the USD61.9/t difference is up to Rp1,137bn of revenue, about a quarter of FY2026E EBITDA, before any pass-through to purchased fruit.
challenges.answer: The cut from 308.27 to 246.36 a tonne is now in the report with its source (S29), quantified as up to 61.91 a tonne of relief, which at our volume and FX is about Rp1,137bn before pass-through to purchased fruit. It is not capitalised in the base case for a sourced reason: the charge resets monthly against a reference price, and the deck's FY2027E path implies a higher reference price than the one that set the November schedule. The full-year upside is carried in valuation.post_bs_review as a stated item rather than as a number in the DCF, and section 5 says so.

challenges.challenge: MSCI's decision is dated (by 30 June 2027, inside the twelve-month window) but is read only as a risk: the report never states the probability or the value of the branch in which Indonesia is not moved to Standalone, the freeze on index increases lifts and the passive bid returns. That is the mirror image of the FTSE deletion and the main upside the lens does not price.
challenges.answer: The no-reclassification branch is now valued rather than treated only as a risk. Section 4 states the MSCI decision date (by 30 June 2027, inside the window), the lifting of the index-increase freeze, and the bull regime value of Rp2,044 a share at the house one-quarter weight, as the mirror image of the FTSE deletion (S24).

challenges.challenge: The deletion is described as 'a scheduled passive seller still to clear' and argued away on liquidity: IDR11.3bn ADV 'across a full year'. Index deletions execute on one effective date, and at IDR11.3bn/day this stock turns only 0.12% of its IDR9.1tn market cap daily: a 1% passive holding is 8 days of ADV and 2% is 16 days, concentrated at the 21 December close. The removal is also permanent rather than a flow that clears, so the base regime's 25% closure is asserted against an unsized, dated seller.
challenges.answer: The deletion is now sized rather than argued away. At a market capitalisation of Rp9.14tn against Rp11.3bn of three-month average daily turnover, each percentage point of the register is about eight sessions of trading, so even a low-single-digit passive weight is weeks of supply concentrated into the 21 December close; band weights are not in the archive, so we bound the line and say so. We keep the base regime as most likely because the absolute rupiah weight is small, but section 4 now calls the closure rate the weakest assumption, and a half-weight-on-bear sensitivity still values the shares above the price (S27, S0).

challenges.challenge: From 2027 palm-oil exports route through PT DSI as sole intermediary against a service fee (news 2026-11-13, material; GAPKI has publicly asked that the fee not burden exporters). That is a new charge on the revenue line in FY2027E, the year that carries most of the DCF, and it appears nowhere in sections 2, 3, 5, the scenarios or the catalysts. The 0.95 wedge has no documented room for it.
challenges.answer: The DSI sole-intermediary regime from 1 January 2027 is now named and sourced (S30). DSI has said the fee will be single-digit dollars a tonne and announced in December 2026, and GAPKI has asked that it not burden exporters; the fee is therefore carried as a visible downside on the FY2027E realisation, not as a modelled number, with a catalyst entry for the December announcement.

challenges.challenge: Net debt is applied two ways. The bridge deducts the 30 September figure of Rp11,125.3bn (pack gross debt 12,029.3 less unrestricted cash 904.0, excluding the Rp3,200bn restricted DHE placement), while the model's own FY2026E path shows gross debt 9,323.1 and net debt 7,518.6, below the 30 September actual by Rp2.7tn, and the headline 1.7x uses that path. A Rp3.6tn move in nine months is a treatment, not 'optimism on deleveraging'. The Rp3,200bn is Rp336/share of DCF equity, about Rp130/share of target.
challenges.answer: Net debt is now on one basis.
